without_fix: Every new or changed test fails and only the guard theory passes. Spec: all 32 cases fail on InMemory and Sqlite and all 192 on SQL Server (6 classes), with join entries left Deleted. Unit: the restore test with the StateChanged sequence, the notification payload test, the complex property test (join Deleted instead of Unchanged) and both SkipCollectionEntryTest.IsModified_tracks_removing_items_from_the_join_table cases fail. Adding_back_skip_navigation_item_does_not_restore_join_entity_when_an_end_is_deleted(deleteCollectionOwner: False/True) passes both with and without the fix.
pr_title: Restore deleted join entity when a skip navigation item is added back
pr_summary_en:
- Bug: removing an entity from a many-to-many skip navigation marks the join entity Deleted; adding the same entity back (e.g. Clear() then re-adding) found that join entry but left it Deleted, so SaveChanges deleted a relationship still present in both collections.
- Fix: on the collection-add path, NavigationFixer restores the join entry with the same state guard as UndeleteDependent (both ends Unchanged or Modified), in a single transition: to Unchanged, or to Modified when properties were already marked as modified before the removal (new internal InternalEntryBase.HasModifiedProperties reads the surviving flags).
- Payload: edits marked as modified before the removal are kept and saved; snapshot-tracked edits are found by the next DetectChanges; as for any Deleted entity, changes made while the join entity was Deleted are not tracked under notification tracking.
- SkipCollectionEntryTest.IsModified_tracks_removing_items_from_the_join_table expected the collection to stay modified after the item was added back, which encoded the bug (the join row was still Deleted); it now expects not modified. As with one-to-many, dependents cascade-deleted from the join entity are not restored.
- Tests: explicit, shared-type, payload and composite-key join entities with remove and Clear(), Modified ends and payload edits (InMemory, Sqlite, SQL Server incl. proxies/TPT/TPC), plus unit tests for notification tracking, a single Deleted -> Unchanged StateChanged event, complex properties on the join entity, and a guard theory where either end is Deleted.
risks: Adds one internal member, Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.ChangeTracking.Internal.InternalEntryBase.HasModifiedProperties (public virtual in the .Internal namespace with the standard internal-API doc comment; virtual because ApiConsistencyTest requires it); no public API outside .Internal changes. Under notification tracking, a property changed while the join entity is Deleted is not preserved (same as any Deleted entity). Under snapshot tracking, payload edits that were never flagged are only picked up by the next DetectChanges (SaveChanges runs it by default); the spec helper calls DetectChanges a second time because the tracking fixture disables AutoDetectChanges. Dependents cascade-deleted from the join entity are not restored (same as one-to-many). SQL Server: the six ManyToManyTracking SQL Server classes were run in full (1398 tests); the rest of the SQL Server suite was not run. The TPT/TPC classes are named TptManyToManyTrackingSqlServerTest and TpcManyToManyTrackingSqlServerTest.
